1.title: Proxy and Target
1.body:
## Recap: setup in 30 seconds

You already set up the proxy in *Web Hacking* (CS101); review it and add the step that was missing,
the certificate to intercept HTTPS:

1. Burp Proxy > Options: listens on `127.0.0.1:8080` (default).
2. Browser: HTTP proxy set to `127.0.0.1:8080` (or FoxyProxy to toggle it on and off).
3. Visit `http://burp` in the browser → Burp's CA certificate → install it as a
   trusted CA (for HTTPS).

## The daily workflow

```text
Browser → Burp Proxy → HTTP History → (analyze) → Repeater → (modify/repeat)
```

- **Intercept ON**: freezes every request so you can edit it LIVE.
- **Intercept OFF** (recommended by default): everything flows freely, but it is SAVED in
  **HTTP History** — review it later with filters.

## Target: the site map

The **Target > Site map** tab builds a tree with ALL the discovered URLs
(through browsing or through fuzzing from Burp). It's your inventory of the target:
- Automatically discovered paths
- Parameters of each endpoint
- Response headers of each URL

Right-click any request in the History → **"Send to Repeater"** (Ctrl+R) or
**"Send to Intruder"** (Ctrl+I) to take it to the next level.

2.title: Repeater
2.body:
## Repeater: the same request, N times, N variations

You receive a request from the History in Repeater and you have TOTAL control:

```http
GET /producto?id=1 HTTP/1.1
Host: tienda.local
Cookie: sesion=abc123
```

You edit `id=1' OR 1=1--` → **Send** → examine the response (status, headers, body).
Edit again → Send. Repeat. Without touching the browser.

### The 4 views of the response

- **Pretty**: formatted (headers on top, body rendered with syntax highlighting)
- **Raw**: exactly as it arrives (bytes in plain text)
- **Render**: as the browser would paint it (for XSS: you see whether your script runs!)
- **Hex**: bytes in hexadecimal (for binaries, encoding issues)

### Real use cases

```text
1. SQLi:  change id=1 → id=1' OR 1=1-- and see if the error changes
2. XSS:   inject <script> into a parameter → Render → does it run?
3. IDOR:  change /perfil/1024 → /perfil/1025 → do you see someone else's data?
4. Auth:  tamper with cookies/tokens → does it accept a modified one?
5. Logic: precio=100 → precio=1 in the cart's POST
```

**Pro shortcut**: right-click any browser request that Burp
captured → "Send to Repeater" → modify → observe. It's 80% of manual web work.

3.title: Intruder
3.body:
## Intruder: from manual to automatic

1. **Send to Intruder** (Ctrl+I) from any request.
2. **Positions**: mark with § what you want to replace:
   ```http
   POST /login HTTP/1.1
   username=§admin§&password=§password123§
   ```
3. **Payloads**: assign lists to each position.
4. **Start attack**: Intruder runs every combination.

### The 4 attack types

| Type | What it does | When |
|---|---|---|
| **Sniper** | one list, one position at a time | testing 1 parameter |
| **Battering ram** | the SAME list in ALL positions | the same password in user and pass |
| **Pitchfork** | parallel lists (user[i], pass[i]) | paired user/password |
| **Cluster bomb** | Cartesian product (every combination) | real brute force |

### The trick: reading the results

Intruder shows a table with every attempt. The key: **sort by Length**.

```text
Payload: password1   Length: 4523   Status: 302   ← redirect (login OK!)
Payload: password2   Length: 4523   Status: 302   ← same... wait
Payload: password3   Length: 4523   Status: 302
Payload: rockyou     Length: 8234   Status: 200   ← DIFFERENT! investigate this one
```

A Length or Status that differs from the general pattern = a different response = a possible success.

### Real Intruder cases

- **Login brute force**: Cluster bomb (users × passwords)
- **Mass IDOR**: Sniper with IDs 1-1000 on /perfil/§id§
- **Parameter fuzzing**: Sniper with XSS/SQLi payloads
- **Rate limit bypass**: Pitchfork with rotated tokens

With Burp mastered (Proxy → Repeater → Intruder), you can test ANY web
application. The next modules in the path apply these techniques against the OWASP flaws
with labs.

burp-suite-pro-t03-q02.prompt: What attack type tests one list one position?
burp-suite-pro-t03-q02.hint: Sniper: one position at a time.

burp-suite-pro-t03-q03.prompt: With 1000 payloads, how do you find successes?
burp-suite-pro-t03-q03.hint: Sort by response length or status.

options.b: By sorting the results by Length or Status: successful ones usually have a response different from the rest
